events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven.** I'd expect it to be the best boat salmon option this week, rated about **3 (good)**.
- **St. Joseph is second, about 2 (average).** It's the backup if Grand Haven is crowded or rough.
- **South Haven and Muskegon are about 1 (below average).** Both were slow last report.
- **At Grand Haven, fish about 120–200 ft of water, with lines around 65–120 ft down.** Run yellow and green meat rigs and green flies, with glow spoons for low light.

## Why

- **Grand Haven:** The Jul 19 Grand Haven report rated boat salmon good (3) with fish 65–120 ft down in 130–220 ft of water.
- **Muskegon and South Haven:** The Jul 19 reports rated Muskegon below average (1), with hit-or-miss action, and South Haven below average (1), with mostly lake trout and some coho.
- **St. Joseph:** The Jul 19 St. Joseph report rated it average (2), though it said the bite was slowing.
- **Live conditions:** I couldn't get live current conditions (the tool returned a backtest summary), so I have no current wind or cold-layer data. I'd expect the ratings to shift if wind or water temperature changed sharply.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (salmon, boat)**
- Grand Haven (2023-07-19): "Boat anglers were catching a mix of salmon and trout 65 to 120 feet down in 130 to 220 feet of water… Yellow and green meat rigs were working well along with green flies." Quality 3. Glow spoons also "produced Chinook salmon" in low light (not rated).
- Muskegon (2023-07-19): "Boat anglers were finding the salmon action to be hit or miss… The best action was 60 to 100 feet down in 110 to 200 feet of water." Quality 1. Glow spoons and green or yellow meat rigs worked.
- South Haven (2023-07-19): "Boat anglers continued to have decent fishing… mostly lake trout with some coho and steelhead." Quality 1. No salmon-specific depth given.
- St. Joseph (2023-07-19): "Boat anglers targeting salmon were catching a few fish in 100 feet of water… The fishing was slowing down." Quality 2.
- Earlier: South Haven (2023-07-05) was quality 1 with fish on spoons; St. Joseph (2023-07-05) was quality 2, with boats fishing beyond 120 ft.

**Past seasons (history, similar water temperature)**
- Past weeks with surface water near 72–75 F ranged from slow (0) to good (3). Grand Haven 2022-08-03 was 2 on green flies and meat rigs at 65–140 ft down; Muskegon 2022-08-03 was 3 with spoons, meat rigs and flies; St. Joseph 2022-08-03 was 3 with meat rigs and spoons.
- Past similar weeks often had the best fish deep, around 100 ft or more.

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water (measured, week before Jul 25): St. Joseph 73 F (buoy 45026), South Haven 73 F (buoy 45168), Grand Haven and Muskegon 71 F (buoy 45161). Those are averages for the week, not today's reading.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are from Jul 19, six days old. Treat the ratings as a guide to what the last reports showed, not as a confirmed bite.
- Live wind and modeled cold-layer data were unavailable, so I can't say whether an upwelling or wind is coming.
- The Grand Haven rating rests on one report, and Muskegon's on one report, so the spread is thin.
- Muskegon and Grand Haven share a buoy, so the water temperature doesn't explain their different ratings. The difference comes from the reports themselves.

## Sources

- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph (Jul 19 bulletin): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/366250d
- St. Joseph and South Haven (Jul 5 bulletin): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/363ad03
- Past-season comparisons: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3268d0b (Aug 3, 2022)
